description.en: Turns a goal (or review gaps) into task-v2 contracts in waves, lints them and has the whole plan critiqued.
description.ru: Превращает цель (или находки ревью) в контракты task-v2 по волнам, линтит и отдаёт план целиком на критику.

plan_sha.note: the signature of the phase plan this run checks (the phase gate admits an approval only for that plan)

extra_rules.note: дополнительные обязательные правила планирования от графа

skip_research.note: the daemon's answer to «research if needed»: on = skip (project setting phase.research switches it off)

validation.note: validation strategy before the plan (project setting phase.validation = on); never on the check path

nodes.prompt: Answer each open 'how' the goal's context leaves unresolved, from the repository and public sources; write the findings as RESEARCH.md text in research_md and a short summary. Read-only.
For each area the goal touches name the closest existing file with file:line and the convention to copy (Grep/Glob, read-only); write them as PATTERNS.md text in patterns_md.

From the phase's CONTEXT.md/SPEC.md write, per requirement and locked decision, the kind of check (test, grep, run, browser) that would fail without the work. For each requirement also list the prohibitions of the spec — what must never happen — and a check that would catch a violation, and name the fixture (the concrete input) for every unsampled edge (empty, maximum, unicode, concurrency) and every prohibition. Output VALIDATION.md text in validation_md.

Produce task-v2 contracts; planning is never done inline in the PM chat. One feature = one task of about 15-60 minutes even across several files; never split by file; a user-visible feature is one end-to-end task.
read_first = files the task changes + source-of-truth files + files whose pattern, signature or convention the change must follow. Every read_first path is a file tracked in git (check with `git ls-files -- <path>`): the writer works in a clean worktree, an untracked file is not there, and the issue lint refuses the contract.
acceptance and verification are commands, greps or file reads naming the exact string, value or exit code; no subjective words (properly, clean, robust, works well, корректно, удобно). In quick or standard quality_mode (the default) acceptance has at most 3 items: with 4 or more, plan-fact fails far more often (hub receipts: 3.5% at 1-3, about a third at 4+). Split the task.
owns_paths must not overlap inside a wave; depends_on only for real output dependencies; at most 8 tasks (more than 3 modules: waves). UI work is a vertical slice with at least one [UI-observable] qa_case per wave.
Locked decisions bind the plan, deferred ones are excluded. extra_rules from the calling workflow are binding. mode=gaps: cluster the gaps by root cause, one task per root cause, sources in order: open findings, verification gaps, review findings.
A task may also carry convergence.criteria (the checks that decide it is done, each a command, a grep or a file read with the exact string, value or exit code; next to acceptance) and files[] ({path, action create|modify|delete, target, change}: the concrete change per file, only files the task owns).

Each task is a task-v2 contract: schema_version 2, id, title, risk (low|medium|high|critical), lane, read_first, owns_paths, never_touch, expected_outputs, interfaces, invariants, out_of_scope, depends_on, acceptance (sentences), verify (none|smoke|tests) and verification as objects {"command": "<one shell command line>", "cwd": "."} - a command, never a sentence about it; every command an acceptance line names is one of them.
When the repository already does what the goal asks (you checked it), return no tasks, already_met true and the evidence in your handoff: an empty plan is then the right answer, not a failure. A fix or a check whose verification already passes on the base is that case: do not dispatch it, the checks close it accepted without a writer. A feature, refactor, docs, chore or research whose checks are already green is not done: those checks prove nothing, so add a check that is red now.
Return also premortem: three to five likely causes this plan fails a week after merge, each one line.
When research_md, patterns_md or validation_md arrive they bind the plan: every task's verification follows the validation strategy, and the code copies the named patterns' conventions.
For every file a task creates, name the closest existing analog in read_first (found with Grep/Glob, read-only) with one line why; a file without an analog says 'no analog' explicitly.
Design discipline: prefer deep modules with narrow interfaces over shallow pass-through wrappers (Ousterhout); slice user-facing work as thin vertical stories (Patton); require idempotency keys and backward/forward schema compatibility on state/RPC boundaries (Kleppmann).

PLAN_CRITIC_METHOD over all tasks together - goals coverage, dependency correctness (no cycle, depends_on names a real task), size, collisions across tasks, boundary violations. A finding without file:line (or PLAN/TASK + field) does not count. Approve the good, not the perfect. Severity is one of critical, high, medium, low, info. A file a task creates with neither an analog in read_first nor an explicit 'no analog' is a finding of severity low: it never changes the verdict by itself, so do not answer rework or block for it alone. Skip this check when plan_sha is set (a plan the PM submitted is checked as it is, the planner cannot add analogs).
